question_en:
The community library is preparing a small display board titled "Why are glaciers in the bay retreating?" Old materials show the attached satellite image. Please answer the following questions:

1. Which glacier is shown in the image, and where is it located? When was the corresponding official thematic report on changes first published, and when was the current public version revised?
2. Review all yearly maps listed in the current public version of this thematic report. Identify the years that meet the following conditions: Dark seawater extends continuously northward from the southern bay in the image, reaching the area between the left glacier branch and the right main trunk, and spreads out to the left and right, forming a T-shaped or wide-headed Y-shaped water body. The horizontally spread part must be wider than the north-south water channel below it. Do not count scattered dark spots, narrow water cracks, cloud shadows, or black areas with missing data. Please list all years that meet the conditions, and provide the total count and the earliest year.

Answer Format: Please answer in separate points numbered (1)–(2); answer both questions in text. For question 1, provide the glacier name, location, and the two dates. For question 2, provide all matching years, the total count, and the earliest year.
answer:
(1) Glacier: Columbia Glacier; Location: The Chugach Mountains in southeastern Alaska, USA, flowing into Columbia Bay of Prince William Sound; Initial publication date of the thematic report: 2012-05-16; Revision date of the current public version: 2026-03-05.

(2) The years meeting the conditions are 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, and 2024, totaling 11 years, with the earliest being 2013.

# Detailed Simulated Retrieval Trajectory · 8-3-E02

## Step 01 · Locate the glacier thematic report using landmarks on the image

Action: Read labels such as West Branch, Main Branch, Medial Moraine, Great Nunatak, and Terminus from the input satellite image, and combine them for the query, rather than searching for any glacier based solely on blue and white colors. Example query: NASA Columbia Glacier West Branch Great Nunatak World of Change.

Evidence Observation: These landmarks match NASA’s feature on changes to Columbia Glacier. The input matches the composition of the 1986 image; West Branch and Main Branch also define the two boundaries used in the subsequent water-area assessment.

Evidence Links:
https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-observatory/world-of-change/columbia-glacier/
https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/esd/eo/woc/images/columbia_glacier/columbia_tm5_1986209.jpg?w=720&h=480&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint

Result of this step: Locked onto Columbia Glacier and the same official year sequence.

## Step 02 · Read location and two different date fields

Action: Review the thematic introduction and machine-readable metadata on the webpage; distinguish between the thematic report publication date, revision date, and the acquisition date of each satellite image.

Evidence Observation: Columbia Glacier is located in the Chugach Mountains of Alaska, USA, flowing into Columbia Bay of Prince William Sound. The saved HTML shows datePublished as 2012-05-16T10:29:00-04:00 and dateModified as 2026-03-05T10:45:51-05:00. The question requires these two page dates, not the year of the 1986 input image.

Evidence Links:
https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-observatory/world-of-change/columbia-glacier/

Result of this step: Use 2012-05-16 and 2026-03-05 for Question 1.

## Step 03 · Fix the public version and enumerate all yearly maps

Action: Extract each year label and its corresponding img address from the saved HTML of the version revised on 2026-03-05, removing header thumbnails, decorative images, and duplicate renderings.

Evidence Observation: This version contains a total of 29 years: 1986, 1987, 1989, 1995, 1996, 1997, 1999, 2000, 2001, 2002, 2003, 2004, 2005, 2006, 2008, 2009, 2010, 2011, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, and 2024. The sequence is not consecutive by year; years such as 1988, 2012, and 2023 do not appear in this closed list and images cannot be self-supplied based on year intervals.

Evidence Links:
https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-observatory/world-of-change/columbia-glacier/

Result of this step: All 29 images enter the screening process and are checked in chronological order.

## Step 04 · Fix image version and maintain the same scale and field of view

Action: Open the 720×480 display rendering for the original src of each yearly image, and verify the sensor/date filename against the webpage year.

Evidence Observation: Links are extracted directly from the saved HTML, retaining parameters such as w=720, h=480, fit=clip, and crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint to avoid switching to other dates or different crop frames. Each image starts from Columbia Bay in the south and tracks northward to the connection between the two branches.

Evidence Links:
https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-observatory/world-of-change/columbia-glacier/
https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/esd/eo/woc/images/columbia_glacier/

Result of this step: The same geometric criteria are applied to all 29 page members.

## Step 05 · Break down T-shaped or wide-headed Y-shaped into visible conditions

Action: First check whether the dark water body is continuous from the southern bay to the north, then check whether the top spreads out to both the left and right, and compare its width with the north-south water channel below it.

Evidence Observation: Four conditions must be met simultaneously: continuous dark seawater, reaching the area between the two branches, spreading left and right, and having a horizontal head wider than the section below. White floating ice, light blue ice-water mixtures, cloud shadows, and black missing-data wedges do not equal visible open seawater; narrow cracks alone or a wide water surface only below are insufficient.

Evidence Links:
https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-observatory/world-of-change/columbia-glacier/

Result of this step: Record specific water body morphology and reasons for exclusion year by year.
